coaching.title: Today's Run
coaching.message: You're 41 days out, in taper, and your recovery score is 81/100 with RHR down to 60—you're fresh. Saturday is your long run anchor, but in taper you dial it back: aim for 90–100 minutes of Z2 (140–150 bpm, conversational pace) on rolling terrain, targeting 1,200–1,400 vert. Skip the hard efforts. This isn't about proving fitness; it's about movement quality, mental confidence on altitude, and keeping your aerobic engine primed without accumulated fatigue heading into race week.

coaching.title: Fuel Right
coaching.message: Your sleep dipped to 7.22h this week—below your 30-day avg of 8.29h—which signals either travel stress or inadequate evening fueling. On a 90–100 minute run, you don't need to carry gels, but eat 30–40g carbs + 10–15g protein within 30 minutes post-run. Tonight: prioritize a carb-forward dinner (rice, pasta, potatoes) with 25–30g protein and salt; hydrate aggressively. Recovery nutrition is your sleep catalyst right now.

coaching.title: Recovery
coaching.message: Sleep efficiency is solid at 88.6%, but total hours are down. The Julian Alps 50K demands 3+ hours of hard concentration and effort in thin air; sleep deprivation amplifies perceived exertion and kills decision-making. Aim for 8–8.5 hours tonight and Sunday night. No caffeine after 2 PM. If you're traveling for work next week, build your recovery protocol now: dark hotel room, white noise, same bedtime, zero screens 30 minutes before sleep.

coaching.title: Mental Edge
coaching.message: In taper, your brain will hunt for reassurance—it always does. You're fit. Your recent vert work (1,568 ft yesterday, 140+ bpm sustained efforts midweek) proves your engine can sustain alpine demands. The next 41 days are about patience, not panic. Use today's long run to visualize the descent into Kranjska Gora and lock in your fueling protocol for hours 3–5, when mental fog hits and nutrition discipline cracks.
